summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia s/p stem cell transplant, multiple compression fractures, and recent cardiogenic shock was admitted for septic shock with fever, chills, and dyspnea. She was treated in the ICU with vasopressors and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to ceftriaxone for a likely urinary source. Imaging revealed right gluteal myositis, confirmed by ultrasound, and no abscess. She developed transient toxic-metabolic encephalopathy after physical therapy, prompting discontinuation of ropinirole due to suspected adverse effects. Her liver enzymes, initially elevated, improved with stabilization. She was transitioned to the floor, completed a seven-day IV antibiotic course, and was discharged to rehabilitation with plans for anticoagulation follow-up, neurology evaluation, and ongoing management of GVHD and diabetes.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
